findings: A1: the brief carries ten of the eleven H2 sections; `## Build plan` is absent. This is deliberate and is not a defect in the brief: generate_instruction.md 2.1 states `## Build plan` is NOT baseline and is emitted only when a variant requests it, and reference/G G.3 describes the same shape. Variant b requested `critical_depth` and `spec_sections` and did not request a build plan, so `spec_sections_given` correctly omits `buildplan`. A1 is stale against that decision; recorded rather than silently marked PASS.

C4: `## UI/UX notes` carries the exact type sizes 16px, 14px, 12px, 20px and 24px, which C4 lists as a numeric recipe. The settled number rule in generate_instruction.md 4 (`The number rule, DECIDED`, A5) supersedes it for TYPE specifically: the exact font family and the exact font size ARE carried, because a font is an identity rather than a value to echo. The brief carries no hex, no millisecond duration, no cubic-bezier and no pinned breakpoint pixel, which are the values that rule does ban. Every other C4 axis is present: palette by role with a contrast requirement, type by personality and role with tabular figures, shape and density by feel, components by their states, motion by character with prefers-reduced-motion respected, a dark mode commitment, and the accessibility and responsive bars.

C5: `## Data model` states each concurrency invariant as an observable property rather than as a named index or constraint, which C5 asks for. INV9 and gate G43 (prescription_lint.py) forbid exactly that vocabulary in `## Technical requirements` and `## Data model`, and generate_instruction.md 4 carries the worked BEFORE/AFTER substitution for it. The mechanical gate and the dated decision win over C5. The rest of C5 holds: derived values are named as derived, and seeding is stated idempotent.

S2: 01-PRD.md lists ten must-have features against S2's band of three to six. reference/G G.2.1 raises the band to six to ten when a companion document was supplied, for the reason recorded there: cutting a companion-backed product to six deletes features the source document specified. Every one of the ten owes a grader and has one, so the obligation that comes with the raised cap is discharged.

S5: 04-uiux-brief.md carries the palette, the motion system and the spacing as words rather than as hex values, millisecond durations and a cubic-bezier, which S5 asks for. The settled number rule (generate_instruction.md 4, A5) bans a hex anywhere in the emitted corpus and G51 checks the inverse: every source colour is described by family, tone and shade. Exact font families and sizes are carried, which is the one exception that rule keeps. S5 is stale against that decision.

S6: 05-backend-schema.md states the critical invariants as observable properties rather than as a named index or constraint. Same cause as QC_instruction C5: INV9 and G43 forbid the storage-engine vocabulary, and the spec folder feeds the brief. The other S6 obligations are present: tables with fields, a `Derived rather than stored` section, and seed data exact enough to assert by value, marked idempotent.

B1: the pattern row for dashboard-analytics names one `user` role; the spec carries three (`owner`, `admin`, `member`). The role-fit rule permits a rename, and this raises the count. Recorded as judgment call 6 in 00-decisions.md: the companion's permission matrix needs three to express an owner who may change the plan, an admin who may not, and a member who may compose a broadcast but not send one. The category modifier is honoured: solo_founder means signup is open and seeded accounts exist for grading.

SCHEMA-011: task.toml carries a `[delivery]` table, which the canonical template in toml_generator.md 11 does not list. It is required by 01-OUTPUT-CONTRACT.md CON-2 and by stage-4-task-toml.md for every new bundle, and validate_task.py (G2) validates its seven keys. Two kit documents disagree; the mechanical gate and the output contract are followed. `[delivery.images]` is deliberately omitted rather than filled with fabricated digests, which ARCH-003 would make a Critical.

BENCH-003: the turns and tokens band cannot be checked against `difficulty`, which holds the mandated empty placeholder. turns_expected 200 and tokens_expected 7500000 sit inside the expert band the row names, which matches the authored scope: ten features, three roles, two slots and a companion-backed brief.

BENCH-005: same cause. `difficulty` is written by calibration, never by the author, so consistency between it and the complexity signals cannot be decided here. The complexity signals themselves are recorded: two service slots, three roles, ten features, variant b, and the standard resource tier.

INT-007: `difficulty` is the empty placeholder, so the three-way consistency between difficulty, the resource tier and the budget is undecidable at authoring time. The tier is Standard and the budget is the expert band; both are internally consistent with each other and with the authored scope.

VERIF-005: `[verifier].env` carries `APP_PUBLIC_URL = "${APP_PUBLIC_URL:-http://localhost:4173}"` exactly as the row and the toml_generator.md 11 template require. Under the new default `environment_mode = "separate"` the grader runs in its own container, where `localhost` is not the app, so the fallback only works if Harbor injects `APP_PUBLIC_URL`. The template was not changed with the mode, so the value is kept and the dependency is recorded here and in the handoff contract rather than guessed at.

CMP-011: the `main` service publishes `4173:4173`. CMP-011 asks for a file free of published host ports, and CMP-022 (Critical) requires `main` to set `ports`. The two rules meet only on `main`, and the Critical one wins. Both sidecars were changed to publish nothing: `postgres` and `mailpit` are reached by service name on the compose network, and the verifier reads the inbox through EMAIL_INBOX_API_URL at http://mailpit:8025, which needs no host publish.
